public_rationale: On February 20, 2026, Bisnow relayed Business Insider's report that lenders declined financing for the CoreWeave-tenanted Lancaster project [e5]. Bisnow also quoted Blue Owl directly denying financing challenges and saying its $500 million bridge commitment remained in place through March [e5]. This disputed account does not establish whether material financing difficulty occurred before March 31, 2026 [e5]. The bridge commitment does not settle whether other planned project debt was difficult to obtain [e5].
limitations: The lender allegations rely on anonymous sourcing relayed through Bisnow; the original report was not verified directly.
No lender correspondence or financing records resolve Blue Owl's denial.
The precise borrower, intended debt package and dates of alleged refusals remain unverified.

our_interpretation: The checkable historical assertion is that the Lancaster project had encountered material difficulty obtaining debt before March 31, 2026.
Calling such difficulty a warning sign is an interpretation, not a separate measurable prediction.
Trouble includes material lender refusals or inability to obtain planned financing. It does not require default or cancellation.
The project's financing partners may be the borrowers even though CoreWeave is the tenant. I therefore distinguish project financing from CoreWeave's general corporate borrowing.
Already supplies an upper date but no beginning date. The target period is left open at the start rather than invented from the reporting.
No debt amount or accounting basis is committed to in the quoted claim.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable project-specific records or sufficiently corroborated reporting establish material lender reluctance, financing delays, or failure to obtain planned debt before publication.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Affirmative project-specific evidence establishes that the alleged financing difficulty did not occur. Later successful financing or the existence of bridge funding alone would not refute earlier difficulty.
